page: Sentinel Roadmap — From L1.5 to Next-Gen Security

current_state.limitation: Static analysis can be evaded via code obfuscation, dynamic module loading, or malicious third-party dependencies.

roadmap.name: Dynamic Analysis in Sandbox (DAST)
roadmap.problem: Static analysis (SAST) can be evaded via code obfuscation, dynamic module loading, or malicious third-party dependencies.
roadmap.solution: Execute each MCP server in an ephemeral, ultra-secure sandbox (gVisor, Firecracker, or WebAssembly). Monitor syscalls during test execution to detect suspicious behavior (e.g., a text formatter trying to read SSH keys or open unexpected network sockets).
roadmap.cost: Free tier available (gVisor is open source, Firecracker is open source). Hosting costs covered when marketplace generates revenue.

roadmap.name: Continuous Supply Chain Audit
roadmap.problem: A server that is secure today can become vulnerable tomorrow if a dependency (npm or pip) suffers a supply chain attack.
roadmap.solution: Automated periodic re-scanning (not just at registration) that checks the dependency tree against vulnerability databases (Snyk, OSV, Socket.dev). If a critical dependency is compromised, the skill status automatically changes from 'auto-scanned' to 'quarantined'.
roadmap.cost: Free tiers available for all. Paid tiers when revenue exists.

roadmap.name: Automated Red Teaming against Prompt Injection
roadmap.problem: Detecting Tool Description Injection (where the skill description tricks the LLM into executing malicious commands) is extremely difficult with static rules.
roadmap.solution: Integrate an adversarial evaluation sub-module with small specialized LLMs. This module systematically 'attacks' tool descriptions using jailbreaking and prompt injection techniques to test whether a reference model (Claude or GPT) deviates from expected behavior when processing the description.
roadmap.cost: Compute costs for LLM inference. Free tier via Groq/Together AI until revenue exists.

roadmap.name: Cryptographic Code Signing
roadmap.problem: A user downloads a skill assuming it is the secure version analyzed by Sentinel, but the source code in the external GitHub repo could have been maliciously modified after analysis.
roadmap.solution: After successful analysis, Sentinel generates a unique hash and signs it cryptographically. The MarketNow platform (or compatible MCP clients) can verify this signature before executing the server locally, ensuring the code has not been altered since the last audit.
roadmap.cost: Free (Sigstore is open source, GitHub attestations are free).

platform_improvements.name: Maintainer-Verified Program Launch
platform_improvements.description: Launch a simplified verification process based on PGP commit signatures or verified developer accounts (GitHub/GitLab verified) plus lightweight KYC. Gives high-trust status to reputable community creators.

platform_improvements.name: Risk Level Classification (Green/Yellow/Red)
platform_improvements.description: Skills are now categorized by system resource access: Green (read-only/static), Yellow (network/APIs), Red (local execution/write). Allows developers to configure granular security policies.

distribution.green: Pure prompts, no install command, no network access
distribution.yellow: Network access, external APIs, or env vars — but no arbitrary code execution

platform_improvements.name: Community Feedback Loop
platform_improvements.description: Decentralized endpoint where MCP clients can anonymously report unexpected behavior, execution failures, or suspected malicious activity. If a tool accumulates multiple reports in a short period, Sentinel prioritizes it for immediate human review.

platform_improvements.name: Advanced Search Filters
platform_improvements.description: Filter by: exact software license, audit status (human-reviewed only), risk level (green/yellow/red), required architecture (Docker, NodeJS, Python).

honest_disclosure: All L2+ features are in design/planning/research phase. None are implemented today. We will not claim they are done until they are. Every status change will be a git commit visible in our public repo.
